precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Remove reset of testtablespace from pg_regress on Windows"
Reverted commit(s): Remove reset of testtablespace from pg_regress on Windows; Lower privilege level of programs calling regression_main
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2b2a070, that moved the reset of path
"testtablespace" used by the regression tests as a path for tablespaces
(via --outputdir) from pg_regress to the MSVC script vcregress.pl, as
this broke the behavior added by ce5d342 to be able to safely run the
regression test suite with an administrative Windows account using a
restricted token.

Note that before 2b2a070, the code doing the reset in pg_regress.c
included a comment telling that we had better move that out to a
different place, leading to the mistake done in 2b2a070.  Fix this
comment, and document instead that we had better never remove this code,
for the sake of not breaking again the behavior we expect on Windows.

Thanks to Thomas Munro and Andrew Dunstan for the discussion.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert support for improved tracking of nested queries
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert support for improved tracking of nested queries
Reverted commit(s): Track more precisely query locations for nested statements; Fix regression with location calculation of nested statements; pg_stat_statements: Add tests for nested queries with level tracking
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts the two following commits:
- 499edb09741b, track more precisely query locations for nested
statements.
- 06450c7b8c70, a follow-up fix of 499edb09741b with query locations.
The test introduced in this commit is not reverted.  This is proving
useful to track a problem that only pgaudit was able to detect.

These prove to have issues with the tracking of SELECT statements, when
these use multiple parenthesis which is something supported by the
grammar.  Incorrect location and lengths are causing pg_stat_statements
to become confused, failing its job in query normalization with
potential out-of-bound writes because the location and the length may
not match with what can be handled.  A lot of the query patterns
discussed when this issue was reported have no test coverage in the main
regression test suite, or the recovery test 027_stream_regress.pl would
have caught the problems as pg_stat_statements is loaded by the node
running the regression tests.  A first step would be to improve the test
coverage to stress more the query normalization logic.

A different portion of this work was done in 45e0ba30fc40, with the
addition of tests for nested queries.  These can be left in the tree.
They are useful to track the way inner queries are currently tracked by
PGSS with non-top-level entries, and will be useful when reconsidering
in the future the work reverted here.

roaster_notes.note: The precedents are coverage-test patches. Most died from author inactivity, which is not a reason against the idea. P8's platform-dependent output and P11's Windows failure do not carry over to deterministic SQL tests in an existing file. One point needs checking in the patch: any non-ASCII input should stay in the encoding-guarded test, because the main test file has no encoding guard.

The patch only adds queries and expected output to the existing fuzzystrmatch regression test. It adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, psql behaviour or dump content, and does not change behaviour for existing users, so the standards and compatibility angle has nothing to object to. Whether the expected output depends on encoding or platform, as in [P8], is a test-level question outside this angle.
The patch changes only the fuzzystrmatch regression test and its expected output. It touches no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or extension API, so this angle has nothing to object to.

The patch only adds test queries and expected output to the fuzzystrmatch regression test. It adds no new function, privilege, default, or code path that users can reach, so there is nothing to object to on security or privilege grounds.

From the maintenance and fit angle, a test-only patch to one contrib module adds no hot-path cost, no API and no lasting commitment beyond keeping one expected output file current. The coverage-test precedents ([P1], [P7], [P8], [P11]) were mostly closed for author inactivity or for platform-dependent output, which is a code-level matter. Two points need a look at the code: whether dmetaphone tests on non-ASCII input make the expected output depend on encoding, and how much the tests add to run time.

The patch only adds regression tests to an existing contrib test file. No existing feature, extension or external tool already provides this test coverage, and the patch adds no second mechanism, so this angle has nothing to raise. Platform or encoding dependence of the expected output is a different angle.

The demand angle has no fair objection here. The patch changes no behaviour and adds no user surface; its only users are developers, and dmetaphone.c at 17.8% line coverage is a real gap in documented, user-facing functions. The [P6] reason, that a test belongs with the change that needs it, was about undocumented behaviour and does not carry over. Run time and platform-dependent output belong to other angles.
